tools.name: get_agenda
tools.description:
Reads back the current state of an agenda, including the id of every block.

Use this when you need block ids you do not already have — for example at the start of
a new conversation where the user has pasted an edit token. After any BriefMe
mutation you already hold current state, so you do not nee

tools.name: update_agenda
tools.description:
Changes the agenda's title. Does not touch any block — use the block tools for those.

Returns the full updated agenda.

tools.name: add_block
tools.description:
Adds one block to an existing agenda. Appends it to the end, or inserts it directly
after after_block_id when you supply one.

Adds only — it does not reorder or change any existing block. Returns the full updated
agenda, so you do not need to call get_agenda afterwards.

tools.name: update_block
tools.description:
Changes one block, identified by block_id. Supply only the fields you want to change —
anything you leave out keeps its current value exactly.

Changes one block only: it does not reorder, add or remove anything. Do not re-send
fields you are not changing, and do not rewrite the whole agenda to make

tools.name: remove_block
tools.description:
Removes one block from an agenda. The remaining blocks keep their ids and their order.

An agenda must keep at least one block, so this fails on the last one. Removing a block
shortens the meeting — it does not redistribute that time to the other blocks.

Returns the full updated agenda.

tools.name: reorder_blocks
tools.description:
Puts the agenda's blocks into the order you give.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "create_agenda" is 2197 chars, far longer than this server's median (306). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "create_agenda" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_agenda · Private data: create_agenda, get_agenda · Public sink: get_agenda, update_block · Destructive: create_agenda, update_block, remove_block, reorder_blocks.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_agenda · Private data: create_agenda, get_agenda · Public sink: get_agenda, update_block · Destructive: create_agenda, update_block, remove_block, reorder_blocks

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
